newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Some Russian warheads to be removed -- ministry.
newsitem.headline: Some Russian warheads to be removed -- ministry.

text.p: Russia will physically remove some of the warheads from its nuclear missiles currently targeted at sites in NATO countries under President Boris Yeltsin's surprise Paris initiative, Russia's defence ministry said on Tuesday.

It said different means will be used to carry out Yeltsin's promise to stop targeting nuclear missiles at NATO states, made by the president earlier on Tuesday after he signed a milestone deal between Moscow and the Western defence alliance in Paris.

"Such means and methods include both measures to de-target missiles and the physical removal of warheads," the ministry's press office said in a statement. "After that, missiles will only be serviced to ensure nuclear safety."

Yeltsin, who joined NATO leaders in signing the "Founding Act on Mutual Cooperation" laying out their relations in the post Cold War world, initially puzzled Western leaders by his pledge to remove warheads from missiles aimed at NATO.

His spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky later explained that Yeltsin actually meant unilaterally extending an agreement not to target nuclear missiles against each other. Moscow has already signed such a pact with the United States and Britain.
"The president means that the warheads will not be targeted at the states which have signed the (NATO-Russia) Founding Act," Yastrzhembsky told reporters.
"In future, the situation is possible when the warheads will be dismantled," he added.
The Defence ministry statement described Yeltsin's initiative, already hailed by the West, as an "additional major step towards building confidence with all NATO countries".
But Interfax news agency quoted a military source as saying that Yeltsin's move was largely symbolic. "Targeting back warheads is a matter of minutes," the unnamed source said.
He added, though, that de-targeting and removal of warheads had its practical side. "Such a step considerably reduces the possibility of an accidental missile launch."
